# Incident Report: 2021-09-10 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.9.10.102 | Sole non-infrastructure host generating C2 traffic |
| MAC | 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3 | ARP replies for 10.9.10.102; matches DHCP client hardware address |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-KKITB6Q | DHCP option 12 (hostname), NBNS name registrations, DNS A queries for `DESKTOP-KKITB6Q.angrypoutine.com` |
| Logged-in user | hobart.gunnarsson | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 10.9.10.102 and DC 10.9.10.9 |
| Domain | angrypoutine.com (DC: 10.9.10.9 / ANGRYPOUTINE-DC) | NBNS, DNS SRV lookups (`_ldap._tcp...dc._msdcs.angrypoutine.com`), LDAP/Kerberos/SMB traffic to 10.9.10.9 |

## Malware Family
**Attribution confidence: behavioral (no signature match performed).**

The infection chain observed is consistent with a **fake browser-update "gate" delivering a DLL-based loader**, followed shortly by **HTTPS command-and-control to VPS infrastructure using a shared self-signed TLS certificate**. This delivery pattern (spoofed old-IE user-agent hitting a randomized-path gate URL, dropping a PE32+ DLL, no client SNI on the follow-on HTTPS C2) matches the family of "fake update" loader campaigns active in this period (e.g., IcedID/SocGholish-style gates); I cannot assert a specific family name with certainty since no string/config extraction or hash/signature lookup was performed (no internet access used, per instructions). Treat the family label as behavioral, not confirmed.

## Timeline of Malicious Activity
1. **t=140.0s** — 10.9.10.102 sends `GET /bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS` to `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206), spoofing User-Agent `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; ...)` — an anachronistic UA (claims IE7 but reports Windows NT 10.0), a strong gate/loader tell.
2. **t=142.2s** — Server (Apache/2.4.6 CentOS, PHP/7.2.34) responds `200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`, 284,816 bytes. Payload extracted via `tshark --export-objects http` is a **PE32+ (x86-64) DLL**.
3. **t=144.3s** (~2s after the DLL lands) — 10.9.10.102 opens TLS 1.2 to **167.172.37.9:443** (DigitalOcean-hosted IP). No SNI sent in ClientHello. Server presents a **self-signed certificate**: CN=`londonareloeli.uk`, O=`LL EST`, OU=`UK System`, L/ST=`London`, C=`UK`.
4. **t=148.7s onward, through t≈4512s** (~73 minutes) — 10.9.10.102 repeatedly reconnects to **94.158.245.52:443**, again with no SNI and the **identical self-signed certificate** (CN=`londonareloeli.uk`). 35 separate SYNs observed at irregular intervals (~5s, ~100s, ~330s, ~360s, ~460s apart) — consistent with C2 beaconing rather than a single user-driven session. Same cert reused across two different IPs indicates shared C2/redirector infrastructure.

## Indicators of Compromise
